title: Level 3 Classical Studies — Analyse Ideas and Values 2025
subject: classical-studies

questions.text:
Answer ONE of the following questions with reference to a classical literary text. You must answer using paragraphs. Characters in classical literary texts may be mythical, fictional, or historical. Support your answer with evidence from a classical literary text. Aim for a concise answer of no more than 5-6 pages.

Question 1: Discuss the extent to which one or more characters exercised their influence to restore stability and/or justice during a period of upheaval.

Question 2: Discuss the extent to which one or more characters acted as a guide or a subordinate.

Question 3: Discuss the ways in which the character of one or more individuals was defined by a sense of loyalty and/or responsibility to their community.

Question 4: Discuss the extent to which one or more characters' commitment to established customs and/or principles was questioned by those around them.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Analyse ideas and values of the classical world by undertaking a methodical examination and interpretation of the ideas and values of the ancient Greeks and/or Romans, as communicated through the literary texts.
- Discuss ideas and values in light of that examination, use primary-source evidence, and draw conclusions.
- The candidate may lack specific detail and aspects may be underdeveloped or omitted.

For Merit:
- Analyse in-depth by undertaking an informed and coherent discussion.
- Use primary-source evidence of specific relevance to the context, explore more than one viewpoint, make comparisons, and draw conclusions supported by primary-source evidence.
- The candidate shows an in-depth understanding of how the literary text reflects the social, political, religious, and/or artistic environment of the time, and draws well-supported conclusions.

For Excellence:
- Analyse with perception by discussing with insight the complexity of ideas and values.
- Establish textual connections, provide critical evaluation, show understanding of wider implications of the analysis, and draw developed conclusions.
- The candidate's response covers all aspects of the question in appropriate depth, with sophisticated discussion that synthesises information.
